store.name: Quillhart
store.tagline: Good paper, fine ink, and letters worth keeping.
store.voice: Warm, courteous and a little old-fashioned, like a shopkeeper writing to a regular customer: full sentences, gentle humor, concrete details (paper weights, nib sizes, cloth and leather), and a fondness for letters and the people who write them. No hype, no exclamation marks, no slang. Says 'we' for the shop and 'you' for the reader.
store.story: Quillhart was opened in 1994 by Nell Hart, a bookbinder, in the old post office on Mercer Street in Hollin Mill, Vermont. The brass mail slots still line one wall and hold envelopes and cards. The shop keeps a small range of paper goods, pens and inks it has tested itself, mixes its own house inks, and wraps every order by hand at a long oak table at the back. All names are invented.

policies.refund: If something isn't right, send it back within 30 days of delivery, unused and in its original wrapping, and we will refund you in full to your original payment method. Opened ink, used notebooks and Card Club months already sent are final sale, unless they arrived damaged, in which case we will replace them at no cost. To start a return, write to hello@quillhart.example with your order number; we will reply within two working days with a return address. Return postage is yours to pay unless we made a mistake.
policies.shipping: We pack and ship orders from our shop in Hollin Mill, Vermont, within two working days. Standard shipping is $6, and free on orders over $60, to anywhere in the United States and Canada. Most US orders arrive in three to six working days, and Canadian orders in five to ten; Canadian orders may owe import duties on arrival. Every order is wrapped by hand in cream tissue and cotton ribbon at no charge. Card Club cards ship on the first working day of each month.
policies.privacy: We collect only what we need to fill and deliver your order and to answer your letters: your name, email address, shipping address and order history. Payments are handled by our payment provider, and we never see or keep your card number. We send our monthly newsletter only if you ask for it, and every issue has a way to unsubscribe. We never sell or share your details with anyone else. To see, correct or delete what we hold about you, write to hello@quillhart.example.
policies.terms: These terms cover purchases from Quillhart, 41 Mercer Street, Hollin Mill, VT 05458. Prices are in US dollars; taxes and shipping are shown at checkout. Many of our goods are made by hand from natural materials, so leather grain, marbling, wood and pressed botanicals vary a little from the photos and from one piece to the next; this is part of their character, not a defect. Card Club subscriptions renew on their schedule until you skip, pause or cancel them from your account. If an item is out of stock after you order, we will write to you and refund it promptly.

art_direction: Real-photo still-life photography for Quillhart, a small, old-fashioned stationery and gift shop. Light: soft window light from the left, morning or late afternoon, gentle warm shadows; never flash or harsh sun. Palette: warm cream and parchment paper tones, deep ink navy, oxblood, moss green, walnut and honey oak, aged brass; muted and warm, never saturated or neon. Surfaces: worn walnut or oak desks, cream linen cloth, cream laid paper; product shots on a seamless warm parchment-colored backdrop. Composition: classic, calm and orderly still life, the subject centered with generous margins so it sits well inside a square or arch-topped picture frame. Lens: 50 to 90 mm, straight on or slightly elevated, shallow depth of field on close details; true texture of paper fibers, book cloth, leather grain, wood and brass. Mood: quiet, homely and timeless, like a well-kept shop on a small-town main street. Paper is always blank, or shows only loose abstract ink swirls and swatches that are not letters. Avoid: any readable text, letters, numbers, handwriting, calligraphy, logos, labels, stamps, brand marks or watermarks; people or faces (hands only when asked); clutter; plastic or CGI look; heavy HDR; oversaturated color.

products.name: Everyday Clothbound Journal
products.description_html:
The notebook we reach for first: a sturdy clothbound journal that lies open on the desk and takes fountain-pen ink without a whisper of bleed-through.

Details

  • A5 (5.8 × 8.3 in), 192 numbered pages
  • Book cloth over boards, rounded corners, cotton ribbon marker
  • Thread-sewn binding that opens flat
  • A paper pocket inside the back cover for letters and receipts

Paper

100 gsm cream wove, smooth enough for a fine nib and heavy enough that ink stays on its own side of the page. Choose 7 mm lines, a 5 mm dot grid, or plain pages.

Care

Wipe the cloth with a barely damp cloth, and keep it out of long hours of direct sun so the color stays true.

attributes.care: Wipe clean with a barely damp cloth; keep out of strong sun.

products.name: Five-Year Line-a-Day Diary
products.description_html:
One page for every day of the year, with room for a few lines on each date for five years running. Turn to today and you will find what you were doing a year ago, and the year before that.

Details

  • 5.3 × 7.5 in, 372 pages with a page for every date
  • Book cloth over boards, gilt-edged pages, two ribbon markers
  • Thread-sewn and rounded at the spine

Paper

80 gsm ivory paper, thin enough to keep the book slim and smooth enough for pencil, ballpoint or a fine fountain pen.

Care

Store it upright on a shelf. A soft brush keeps dust off the gilt edges.

attributes.care: Store upright; brush dust from the gilt edges.

products.name: Marbled Edition Journal

A small run of journals bound in hand-marbled paper, each cover pulled from the bath one sheet at a time, so no two are alike. We make a few dozen each season and they rarely last the month.

Paper

120 gsm cream laid paper with a soft ribbed texture, lovely under a broad nib.

Care

Marbled paper is delicate: keep it dry, and away from long hours of sun.

attributes.care: Keep dry and out of strong sun.

products.name: Refillable Leather Journal

A wrap of thick vegetable-tanned leather that holds up to three slim notebooks under elastic bands, closed with a long cord. The leather darkens and softens with years of handling; the notebooks inside come and go.

Details

  • Comes with one lined, one dot-grid and one plain insert
  • Cut, stitched and edge-burnished by hand

Paper

Each insert has 64 pages of 90 gsm cream paper, stitched into a kraft cover. Refills are sold in our Pocket Notebook Trio.

Care

Rub in a little leather balm twice a year. Scratches buff out with a warm thumb.

attributes.care: Leather balm twice a year; buff scratches by hand.

products.name: Ledger Brass Fountain Pen
products.description_html:
A solid brass fountain pen with a steel nib, weighty enough to steady the hand and small enough for a shirt pocket. It arrives bright and slowly takes on a warm, honeyed patina.

Details

  • Polished steel nib in extra fine, fine, medium or broad
  • Takes standard international cartridges or the included converter
  • Comes in a cotton pouch with three cartridges of Harbor Blue-Black

Care

Flush the nib with cool water when you change inks. Polish the brass back to bright with a soft cloth, or leave the patina be.

attributes.care: Flush with cool water between inks; polish brass with a soft cloth.

products.name: Quillhart House Ink, 50 ml
products.description_html:
Our own fountain-pen inks, mixed in small batches in five colors we couldn't find anywhere else: quiet, well-behaved shades that shade nicely and dry in good time.

Details

  • 50 ml in a squat glass bottle with a wide neck, so the last drops still reach the nib

  • Dries in about 15 seconds on our journal paper

Colors

Harbor Blue-Black for letters, Oxblood for notes in the margin, Fern and Walnut for journals, and Slate for everything else.

Care

Keep the cap tight and the bottle out of the sun. Flush your pen with water before changing colors.

attributes.care: Cap tightly; store away from sun; flush pens between colors.

pages.title: Our story
pages.content_html:
Quillhart opened in the spring of 1994 in the old post office on Mercer Street, in Hollin Mill, Vermont. Nell Hart, a bookbinder who had spent ten years repairing other people's books, wanted a shop for the things she used every day at her own bench: good paper, honest pens, ink that behaved itself, and something nice to wrap it all in.

The brass mail slots are still on the north wall. These days they hold envelopes and cards instead of letters, and the sorting table at the back has become our wrapping table.

What we keep

We keep a small range on purpose. Every notebook is tested with fountain-pen ink, page by page, before it reaches the shelf. Every pen is filled and written with at the counter. Our five house inks are mixed in small batches in the back room, and our journals are bound by a two-person bindery we have worked with for twenty years.

Why letters

A letter takes longer than a message and lasts much longer too. We have watched customers buy a single card for a friend and come back years later for a box of fifty. We think the world is a little kinder with more letters in it, and we would like to help you write a few.

Come and see us

The shop is open Tuesday to Saturday, 10 to 5, and Sunday 11 to 4. There is always a pen to try and, most afternoons, a pot of tea on the counter.

pages.title: Shipping & returns
pages.content_html:
Shipping

We pack and ship every order from the shop within two working days, wrapped by hand in cream tissue and tied with cotton ribbon.

  • Standard shipping is $6 to the United States and Canada.
  • Shipping is free on orders over $60.
  • Most US orders arrive in three to six working days; Canadian orders in five to ten.
  • Canadian orders may owe import duties on delivery.

Card Club cards ship on the first working day of each month, or of each season if you chose seasonal delivery.

Gift notes

Add a note at checkout and we will write it out by hand on one of our cards and tuck it in the parcel. We leave prices out of every gift order.

Returns

If something isn't right, send it back within 30 days of delivery, unused and in its original wrapping, for a full refund. Opened ink and used notebooks can't come back, unless they arrived damaged; then we will replace them at no cost.

To start a return, write to hello@quillhart.example with your order number, and we will send the return address. Refunds go back to your original payment method within five working days of the parcel reaching us. You can read our full refund policy as well.

pages.title: Questions
pages.content_html:
Will your notebooks take fountain-pen ink?

Yes. Every notebook and letter set we stock is tested with a medium nib and our own house ink before it goes on the shelf. The product pages say how heavy each paper is; anything 90 gsm or above handles most inks without bleeding through.

I have never used a fountain pen. Where should I start?

The Schoolroom Fountain Pen and our Ink Sampler. The pen is light and forgiving, and the sampler lets you try all five house inks before choosing a bottle. Our journal has a short guide to choosing a first pen.

Do you gift wrap?

Every order is wrapped by hand at no charge. Add a note at checkout and we will write it on one of our cards, and we never put prices in a gift parcel.

How does the Card Club work?

Choose monthly or seasonal delivery, and four new letterpress cards arrive with their envelopes. You can skip a delivery, pause or cancel any time from your account.

Can I visit the shop?

Please do. We are at 41 Mercer Street in Hollin Mill, open Tuesday to Saturday, 10 to 5, and Sunday 11 to 4.

posts.title: Choosing a first fountain pen
posts.content_html:
Most people who come to the counter asking about fountain pens are worried about two things: that it will be difficult, and that it will be messy. It is neither, if you start with the right pen.

Start with a medium steel nib

Steel nibs are sturdy and forgiving, and a medium nib glides over most papers without catching. Fine nibs suit small handwriting; broad nibs show off an ink's color but need better paper. Gold nibs are lovely, but there is no need to begin with one.

Cartridges first, bottles later

Cartridges are clean and simple. Once you have a favorite color, a converter lets you fill from a bottle, which is cheaper and offers far more shades.

Mind the paper

A good pen on thin copy paper will feather and bleed. Try it on a notebook of 90 gsm or more and you will see what all the fuss is about.

Use it every day

A fountain pen likes to be used. Write a list, a note, a page of your diary. If it sits for a few weeks, rinse the nib under cool water and it will be as good as new.

posts.title: The art of the thank-you note
posts.content_html:
A thank-you note does not need to be long. It needs to be specific, sincere and sent while the gift is still fresh in everyone's mind. Here is the simple shape we have recommended at the counter for thirty years.

Name the thing

Say what you are thanking them for, plainly. A scarf, an evening, a kindness in a hard week.

Say how you use it

Tell them where the scarf has been, or what you have been cooking from the book. This is the line they will remember.

Look forward

End with something ahead: the next visit, the spring, the next time you will see them.

Then send it

Within a week is ideal, but a late note is far better than none. Keep a box of cards and a book of stamps in the same drawer, and you will find it much easier to sit down and write.

posts.title: Keeping a line-a-day diary
posts.content_html:
A journal can feel like homework. A line-a-day diary asks for only a few sentences, and after a year it begins to give something back: each page shows you the same date a year before, and the year before that.

Keep it where you sit at night

On the nightstand, by the kettle, beside the armchair. The diary that is within reach is the one that gets written in.

Write the small things

The weather, what you ate, who called, what made you laugh. The ordinary details are the ones you will be most glad of later.

Don't worry about missed days

Leave the space blank and pick up again tonight. Five years is long enough to forgive a few gaps.

Read back on birthdays

Once a year, read the whole page for your birthday. It is the best present the diary gives.

note.heading: Why we still write letters
note.letter:
When we opened in the old post office in 1994, people told us letters were on their way out. Thirty-odd years later, the brass mail slots on our north wall are still full, now with envelopes and cards for you to fill.

We keep a small range on purpose. Every notebook is tested with real ink, every pen is filled and tried at the counter, and every order is wrapped by hand at the long table at the back. We hope something here sends a few more letters out into the world.
